standards_mappings.rationale: Backs SWE.2 with a real interface specification: providing and consuming module, the real C signature transcribed from the header at 308028fb, per-parameter direction, unit, meaning and valid range with the mechanism that enforces it, a return contract whose values are the enumerators the source defines, validity signalling read off the real error paths, timing where the source imposes one, concurrency, and a required not_specified_by_source list. Three elements: the initialiser and the two aggregate validators, over a boundary whose interface is almost entirely parameterless. The status stays partially_mapped: the whole family remains a reconstruction of an existing implementation rather than the product of an architectural design activity, and Component Design remains absent.

providing_module.name: Redundancy management module, MRC
providing_module.role: Owns the validity of every measured quantity in a redundant system. It reads the base and redundancy-0 database tables, compares them quantity by quantity, and sets a per-quantity validity flag that the safe-operating-area and diagnosis modules then act on. It is the element that turns two independent measurement chains into a single trusted value or into a declared disagreement.

consuming_modules.name: Safe-operating-area supervision and diagnosis modules
consuming_modules.consumption_evidence: The validity flags this module publishes are what the SOA and diagnosis layers consume; the SOA record FB2-SW-DSN-000002 and the diagnosis interface FB2-SW-IFS-000006 both depend on measurement validity, and the anchor FB2-SRC-COD-000031 records this module at src/app/application/redundancy/redundancy.c L658-L673.

elements.consuming_module: Startup, before the cyclic tasks run

values.STD_OK: The validity tables were initialised; the return is STD_OK only after every string, module and cell block has been marked invalid.
values.STD_NOT_OK: Not reached in the source: the function initialises every entry and returns STD_OK.

return_contract.default_on_no_information: A void-in/void-out initialiser that must run before any measurement is trusted returns a verdict the source never computes a negative for, so a caller that checks it is checking an always-true value.
return_contract.evidence: STD_RETURN_TYPE_e has exactly two members, STD_OK and STD_NOT_OK, declared at src/app/main/include/fstd_types.h L82-L85. The return is retval at src/app/application/redundancy/redundancy.c L1108; the initialisation loop runs to src/app/application/redundancy/redundancy.c L1107.

validity_signalling.mechanism: Return value STD_RETURN_TYPE_e. The verdict is a formality: the source sets retval to STD_NOT_OK at src/app/application/redundancy/redundancy.c L1082 and changes it to STD_OK unconditionally on completing the loops.
validity_signalling.evidence: src/app/application/redundancy/redundancy.c L1082 and the return at L1108.

timing.evidence: Called once at start-up, not periodically.

concurrency.evidence: A start-up initialiser; not re-entrant because it writes module-static tables without a lock and the source does not guard it.

error_paths.observed_behaviour: The function always completes and returns STD_OK; no error path in the source returns a negative.

not_specified_by_source: The interface does not state that it must run before any measurement is consumed, and nothing in the return value reports that it was skipped.
It does not state what the validity flags are set to if it is never called, so an uninitialised start-up and a successful one are indistinguishable to a reader of the interface.

The body marks every cell invalid at src/app/application/redundancy/redundancy.c L1084-L1090; the interface does not say that a fresh start-up therefore reports every measurement invalid until the first validation cycle runs.

elements.consuming_module: The cyclic task that runs the redundancy check

values.STD_OK: Every cell voltage and cell temperature agreed between the base and redundancy-0 chains, so retval stayed STD_OK.
values.STD_NOT_OK: At least one cell voltage or cell temperature disagreed; retval is set to STD_NOT_OK at src/app/application/redundancy/redundancy.c L1147.

return_contract.default_on_no_information: One negative covers every disagreement across every cell of every string. The interface returns no indication of which cell failed or how far apart the two chains were; the per-cell detail is published in the database, not returned here.
return_contract.evidence: STD_RETURN_TYPE_e has exactly two members, STD_OK and STD_NOT_OK, declared at src/app/main/include/fstd_types.h L82-L85. The comparison is delegated to MRC_ValidateCellVoltageMeasurement and MRC_ValidateCellTemperatureMeasurement at src/app/application/redundancy/redundancy.c L1133 and L1137, and the aggregated verdict is returned at L1149.

validity_signalling.mechanism: Return value STD_RETURN_TYPE_e carrying an aggregate verdict. Per-cell outcomes are not returned; they are written to the database tables this function reads.
validity_signalling.evidence: The aggregate is the return at src/app/application/redundancy/redundancy.c L1149; the per-quantity flags are the mrc_tableCellVoltages and mrc_tableCellTemperature entries.

timing.evidence: Not periodic by itself. It is a database read followed by a comparison; the cadence on which a caller repeats it is not stated at this boundary.

concurrency.evidence: Called from a task; it reads the database through DATA_READ_DATA and writes module-static tables, holding no lock of its own.

error_paths.condition: a cell voltage disagrees between the two chains
error_paths.observed_behaviour: retval becomes STD_NOT_OK and the function still writes the per-cell validity flags.

error_paths.condition: a cell temperature disagrees between the two chains
error_paths.observed_behaviour: Same: aggregate STD_NOT_OK, per-cell flags written.

not_specified_by_source: The interface returns no parameters, so a caller cannot ask about one string or one module; the whole system is validated or nothing is.
It does not return the deviation magnitude or which cells failed; that detail is only in the database, so a caller must go round again to learn why.
The interface does not state the tolerance each comparison uses; those live in the per-quantity validators this function delegates to.

The two module-static tables it declares at src/app/application/redundancy/redundancy.c L1115-L1122 shadow the database tables of the same unique id, which the header does not explain and a reader of this interface would not expect.

elements.consuming_module: The cyclic task that runs the redundancy check

values.STD_OK: Current, string voltage, battery voltage and high-voltage-bus measurements all passed their validity checks.
values.STD_NOT_OK: At least one pack-level quantity failed; packMeasurementValidity is returned as STD_NOT_OK.

return_contract.default_on_no_information: One negative covers four independent pack quantities, so a current-sensor failure and a high-voltage-bus failure are indistinguishable to the caller.
return_contract.evidence: STD_RETURN_TYPE_e has exactly two members, STD_OK and STD_NOT_OK, declared at src/app/main/include/fstd_types.h L82-L85. The four validators are called at src/app/application/redundancy/redundancy.c L1161-L1164 and the aggregate is returned at L1169.

validity_signalling.mechanism: Return value STD_RETURN_TYPE_e carrying an aggregate verdict over four quantities.
validity_signalling.evidence: The aggregate is the return at src/app/application/redundancy/redundancy.c L1169; the per-quantity detail is written into the mrc_tablePackValues table at src/app/application/redundancy/redundancy.c L1167.

timing.evidence: Not periodic by itself; a database read followed by four checks.

concurrency.evidence: Called from a task; reads the database, holds no lock.

error_paths.condition: a pack quantity fails its validity check
error_paths.observed_behaviour: The aggregate return becomes STD_NOT_OK; the failing quantity is not identified.
error_paths.evidence: src/app/application/redundancy/redundancy.c L1161-L1164 and the return at L1169.

not_specified_by_source: As with the AFE element, the interface takes no parameter and returns no detail, so the caller cannot isolate which of the four quantities failed.
It does not state the tolerance or the age limit each pack check applies.

It does not distinguish a measurement that has never been taken from one that has gone stale, although MRC_MeasurementUpdatedAtLeastOnce at src/app/application/redundancy/redundancy.c L1172 is the helper that would make that distinction internally.

interface_level_gaps.gap: Neither validation element returns which quantity failed or by how much; both return a single aggregate verdict.
interface_level_gaps.consequence: A caller that receives STD_NOT_OK cannot act on the specific quantity from the return value alone and must read the database to find out, so the interface is not self-sufficient for diagnosis.
interface_level_gaps.evidence: MRC_ValidateAfeMeasurement returns one retval at src/app/application/redundancy/redundancy.c L1149 and MRC_ValidatePackMeasurement one packMeasurementValidity at L1169, over respectively every cell and four pack quantities.

interface_level_gaps.gap: Both validation elements take no parameters and expose no per-quantity entry point.
interface_level_gaps.consequence: The redundancy check is all-or-nothing through this interface, so a consumer that needs the validity of one quantity must either run the whole check or reach into the database directly.
interface_level_gaps.evidence: The declarations at src/app/application/redundancy/redundancy.h L143 and L152 take void, and the bodies at src/app/application/redundancy/redundancy.c L1111 and L1152 read fixed tables.

revision_history.author: sw_engineer
revision_history.description: Three elements over the redundancy-management boundary, read from redundancy.h and redundancy.c at 308028fb. This is the second independent barrier the safety case names: it compares the base measurement chain against the redundancy-0 chain and publishes a validity flag per measured quantity. Its interface is almost entirely free of parameters, because it reads the database itself, and that shapes what a caller can and cannot do with it.
